scenario: A regional bakery produces exactly six breads — focaccia, hearth loaf, kaiser rolls, multigrain, pumpernickel, and sourdough — in a single morning. The breads are baked one at a time, in six consecutive batches numbered 1 through 6. Each bread is assigned to one of two product lines, the Rustic line or the Sandwich line. The schedule must conform to the following conditions: Exactly three breads are on the Rustic line. Sourdough and focaccia are on the same line. Hearth loaf and multigrain are on different lines. Pumpernickel is baked earlier than sourdough. Kaiser rolls are baked in an earlier batch than multigrain. Multigrain is baked immediately before or immediately after hearth loaf.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order in which the breads are baked, from batch 1 through batch 6?

choices.label: A
choices.text: sourdough, pumpernickel, kaiser, multigrain, hearth, focaccia

choices.label: B
choices.text: kaiser, pumpernickel, multigrain, hearth, focaccia, sourdough

choices.label: C
choices.text: pumpernickel, kaiser, focaccia, hearth, sourdough, multigrain

choices.label: D
choices.text: pumpernickel, multigrain, kaiser, hearth, focaccia, sourdough

choices.label: E
choices.text: focaccia, pumpernickel, sourdough, multigrain, kaiser, hearth

explanations.correct: B satisfies every rule: pumpernickel (2) precedes sourdough (6); kaiser (1) precedes multigrain (3); and multigrain (3) is immediately before hearth (4).
explanations.A: Sourdough (1) is baked before pumpernickel (2), violating the rule that pumpernickel precedes sourdough.
explanations.C: Multigrain (6) is not adjacent to hearth (4); they must be in consecutive batches.
explanations.D: Kaiser (3) is baked after multigrain (2), violating the rule that kaiser precedes multigrain.
explanations.E: Sourdough (3) is baked before multigrain and kaiser, but kaiser (5) must come before multigrain (4) — here kaiser is actually after multigrain, violating that rule.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kaiser rolls are baked in batch 1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sourdough is baked in batch 6.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Multigrain is baked in batch 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked earlier than kaiser rolls.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Multigrain is baked earlier than sourdough.

explanations.correct: Kaiser precedes multigrain, and multigrain is adjacent to hearth. Sourdough must be preceded by pumpernickel, and once kaiser, pumpernickel, multigrain, and hearth all occupy earlier batches in every valid arrangement, sourdough ends up later than multigrain. In every verified solution, multigrain's batch number is lower than sourdough's.
explanations.A: Kaiser can be in batch 1, 2, or 3 — pumpernickel or focaccia can also occupy batch 1.
explanations.B: Sourdough can be in batch 5 (with focaccia in 6).
explanations.C: Multigrain can be in batch 3, 4, or 5.
explanations.D: Kaiser can be in batch 1 with pumpernickel later; this is not required.

questions.questionStem: If focaccia is baked in batch 1, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Multigrain is baked in batch 3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hearth loaf is baked in batch 6.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked in batch 4.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Kaiser rolls are baked in batch 3.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Sourdough is baked in batch 4.

explanations.correct: With focaccia at 1, one valid arrangement is focaccia–kaiser–pumpernickel–multigrain–hearth–sourdough, placing kaiser in batch 3.
explanations.A: With focaccia at 1, kaiser and pumpernickel must fit in batches 2 and 3 before sourdough at 6, and multigrain/hearth occupy 4 and 5; multigrain cannot be at 3.
explanations.B: Sourdough must be at 6 when focaccia is at 1 (since focaccia and sourdough share a line, and sourdough needs pumpernickel earlier plus kaiser→multigrain→hearth earlier). Hearth at 6 is impossible.
explanations.C: With focaccia at 1 and sourdough at 6, pumpernickel must be in batches 2 or 3, not 4 — batches 4 and 5 are taken by the multigrain/hearth pair.
explanations.E: Sourdough must be in batch 6 in this case, not 4.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hearth loaf is baked in batch 3.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked in batch 3.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Kaiser rolls are baked in batch 1.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sourdough is baked in batch 2.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Focaccia is baked in batch 5.

explanations.correct: Pumpernickel must be baked before sourdough, so sourdough cannot be in batch 2 — that would leave only batch 1 for pumpernickel, but kaiser must also precede multigrain, and multigrain must be adjacent to hearth. Working through all such arrangements, sourdough at 2 is impossible.
explanations.A: Hearth can be in batch 3 (with multigrain in 4).
explanations.B: Pumpernickel can be in batch 3 (e.g., focaccia, kaiser, pumpernickel, multigrain, hearth, sourdough).
explanations.E: Focaccia can be in batch 5 (with sourdough in 6).

questions.questionStem: If pumpernickel is baked in batch 1, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kaiser rolls are baked in batch 2.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sourdough is baked in batch 6.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Focaccia is baked in batch 5.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Multigrain is baked in batch 4.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Hearth loaf is baked in batch 3.

explanations.correct: If pumpernickel is in batch 1, kaiser must precede multigrain, and multigrain–hearth occupy an adjacent pair later. Focaccia/sourdough must both appear. Kaiser is forced into batch 2 in every arrangement where pumpernickel occupies batch 1.
explanations.B: Sourdough can be in batch 5 (with focaccia at 6).
explanations.C: Focaccia can be in batch 3 or 6, not only 5.
